Unscroll shows you how long you spend in Instagram, TikTok and Facebook, while you\'re spending it. You choose limits, and it adds a little friction to help you stop.
Private by design: everything stays on this phone. No account, no ads, no tracking.
Next, we\'ll ask for a few permissions and explain why each one is needed.
Usage Access lets Unscroll notice when Instagram, TikTok or Facebook is on your screen, so it can time your sessions.
Unscroll only sees app names and times. It never sees what you look at, type or watch, and nothing leaves your phone.
Tap Open settings, find Unscroll in the list, turn on \"Permit usage access\", then come back here.
Display over other apps lets Unscroll show a small timer while you scroll, and a block screen when you reach a limit you set.
This only lets Unscroll draw on the screen. It can\'t read anything that other apps show.
Tap Open settings, turn on \"Allow display over other apps\", then come back here.
Notifications let Unscroll show that it\'s running, and send nudges like break reminders.
Tap Allow notifications. If nothing pops up, Unscroll opens its notification settings so you can turn them on there.
Some phones close apps in the background to save battery. When that happens, Unscroll stops timing your sessions without telling you.
Unscroll only does work while a tracked app is open and the screen is on, so turning off battery optimization costs very little battery.
Tap Open settings, switch the list to \"All apps\", choose Unscroll and pick \"Don\'t optimize\" (or \"Unrestricted\").
Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO: open App info, turn on Autostart, then set Battery saver to \"No restrictions\". Also lock Unscroll in the recent apps screen (pull its card down or long-press it).
Samsung: go to Settings, then Battery, then Background usage limits. Remove Unscroll from \"Sleeping apps\" and \"Deep sleeping apps\", and add it to \"Never sleeping apps\".
Huawei and Honor: go to Settings, then Battery, then App launch. Find Unscroll, switch it to \"Manage manually\" and turn on Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background.
OnePlus: open App info, then Battery, and choose \"Allow background activity\" or \"Unrestricted\". Also lock Unscroll in the recent apps screen.
Other phones can have their own battery savers. dontkillmyapp.com has steps for most brands.

Counts how many times you swipe in Instagram, TikTok and Facebook, so Unscroll can show your swipe count, suggest a break, and cover the app when your swipe limit is reached. It does not read your screen, messages or anything you type, and nothing leaves your phone. Optional: turn it off any time.

Unscroll can count how many times you swipe in the apps you choose. You\'ll see the count on the timer and the dashboard, you can ask for a break after a number of swipes, and you can set a swipe limit that covers the app when you reach it.

It uses Android\'s Accessibility Service to notice that a scroll happened in Instagram, TikTok or Facebook, and in which of these apps. It counts, and it can cover the screen when your swipe limit is reached. It doesn\'t look at any other app.

It does not read your screen, posts, messages, usernames or anything you type. It does not tap or type anything for you; the only thing it can do is send you to the home screen when your own swipe limit is reached. It does not send data anywhere: the counts stay on this phone, and Unscroll has no account and no internet access for this.
Everything else in Unscroll works without it. You can turn it off at any time in Settings, or in your phone\'s Accessibility settings.
If you agree, Unscroll opens Accessibility settings. Find \"Unscroll swipe counter\" there and switch it on.
On Android 13 and later, apps that weren\'t installed from an app store can\'t switch on an accessibility service until you allow it. To allow it:
